newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-NEW MATCH-FIXING ALLEGATION AGAINST ANDERLECHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW MATCH-FIXING ALLEGATION AGAINST ANDERLECHT.

text.p: A Belgian charged with blackmail in connection with match-fixing allegations surrounding a 1984 UEFA Cup tie said on Friday Belgian club Anderlecht had asked him to rig another Cup match as well.
Anderlecht has denied the allegations. But the turmoil over the affair on Friday caused its supervisory board to put any discussion on plans to seek a bourse listing on ice.

The man charged, Jean Elst, said in an open letter to Belgian radio and television stations that in addition to the semifinal between Anderlecht and Nottingham Forest, Anderlecht had also asked him to bribe the referee of another Cup tie.
"Apart from this match (Anderlecht v Nottingham) I was earlier approached by Anderlecht to try and buy the match against Banik Ostrava in the framework of the same UEFA Cup," Elst said in the letter.
Anderlecht took the second-round tie against Banik 4-2 on aggregate, winning 2-0 and drawing 2-2.
His lawyer, Michel Dillen, told Reuters by telephone the letter was genuine and that his client would be presenting evidence on the allegations next week. He gave no details.
Elst said in his letter: "The referee made it clear to me that Anderlecht should consider itself lucky that he would not report this request to UEFA."
Elst said Anderlecht had given him 100,000 Belgian francs to try and bribe the referee.

Elst and another Belgian, Rene Van Aeken, were charged earlier this week with blackmail, the Brussels public prosecutor's office said on Thursday. They had been released, with certain conditions attached, pending the investigation.
Elst said: "I wish to make it clear that Mr R Van Aeken had nothing to do whatsoever with these bribery cases."

Police launched a probe into the allegations after Anderlecht said it had been blackmailed by two men. One of the men claimed to have acted as an intermediary to fix the second leg which Anderlecht won 3-0 after losing the first leg 2-0.
The result, after a disputed penalty for the Belgians and a disallowed Forest goal, took Anderlecht to the final which they lost to another English club, Tottenham.
Anderlecht confirmed police were asked to investigate the alleged blackmail attempt, but denied the central allegation that the club used an intermediary to try to "buy" the game.
"Thirteen years ago I bribed the Spanish referee in charge of the UEFA Cup match between Anderlecht and Nottingham," Elst said in Thursday's edition of Belgian paper Het Laatste Nieuws.
There is no suggestion made in the allegations that Nottingham Forest players or officials were involved.
Anderlecht, who meet Internazionale Milan in the UEFA quarter-finals in two weeks, have declined to comment further.
UEFA's disciplinary committee is studying a file on the various allegations, received on Wednesday.

Anderlecht club manager Michel Verschueren told Belgian BRTN radio on Friday that the "unforeseen and spectacular events...what I would call the Elst case" had kept the supervisory board from discussing a possible stock market listing of the club at its meeting on Thursday.
Originally, a decision had been due by Easter.
The club, now owned by the Vanden Stock family, had been considering tapping the bourse to strengthen itself and to preserve its standing in European soccer.
